resources.string: Robot sends your search words to the service, reads what it finds and answers with numbered sources. Tap one to set it up.
Free, nothing to set up: Robot opens your browser at the engine\'s own search page and never sees the results. Your browser sends your words, with its cookies. Tap one to make it the default.

Say “search DuckDuckGo for …” or « cherche sur Startpage … » to use one; “search in my browser for …” uses the default, and so does “search the web for …” while Robot\'s own web search is off. When the model writes the words (“look it up on Google”), a card shows them first. Startpage is the default: Google\'s results without Google seeing you, and by its policy it records neither your IP address nor your searches, under Dutch and EU law. DuckDuckGo is as private by its policy, but most of its results are Bing\'s and it is a US company.

Privacy levels, from each one\'s own policy (checked 12 October 2026). High: your words aren\'t kept with your IP address or an account, and no profile is made of them. Medium: they go with your IP address (or part of it, or an account) to a company that keeps them for weeks or months, with no ad profile unless you agree. Low: your searches are kept with you and used for ads, or a stranger\'s server sees them.
Until then Robot\'s own web search says it can\'t check the news, and “search the web for …” opens your browser instead.

Google\'s results, fetched without your IP address or cookies. Records neither your IP address nor your searches, no tracking cookies (its policy). Dutch company, part-owned by System1, a US ad company.
Mostly Microsoft Bing\'s results, with its own crawler. Doesn\'t save your searches; uses your IP address only for the moment; ads from your words only (its policy). US company.
Its own independent index. Keeps search words without your IP address and makes no profile (its policy). US company (Brave Software).
Its own independent index. Replaces your IP address with a country code in its logs and sets no cookies (its policy). UK company.
Its own index (Staan, with Ecosia) and Microsoft Bing. Your words and part of your IP address go to Microsoft, kept 6 months; ad profiles only if you agree. French company.
Microsoft Bing\'s results, Staan\'s, and Google\'s if you agree. Your words and IP address go to Microsoft (kept 6 months) or Google (9 months). German company.
Its own index, the largest. Keeps your searches with your IP address and cookies, ties them to your Google account when you\'re signed in, and uses them for ads. US company.
Its own index. Keeps your searches with your IP address and cookies, ties them to your Microsoft account when you\'re signed in, and uses them for ads. US company.
Your own server asks the engines for you, without cookies: they see your home\'s IP address, and nobody else sees your words. Free (your hardware).
About 1.2¢ a search, with your key. Doesn\'t store API searches against your account or build a profile (its policy). US company.
Its own index. Free monthly credit (about 1,000 searches) with your key and a card on file. Keeps your searches 90 days with your API account. US company.
Its own index, with your key (through Mojeek\'s sales contact), about 0.2p a search. No tracking (its policy). UK company.
Free. A stranger\'s server: they see your words and the phone\'s IP address, and no policy binds them. SearXNG asks Google, DuckDuckGo, Startpage, Bing… for you. Many refuse apps.
Free, no account: facts from Wikipedia, no general web search. Wikimedia keeps the phone\'s IP address in its logs for up to 90 days; no ads, no profile.
Free, no account: DuckDuckGo\'s official short answers, often from Wikipedia, not a list of results; the card credits DuckDuckGo. Doesn\'t save your searches (its policy). US company.
Robot opens %1$s in your browser with these words: your browser sends them, and Robot doesn\'t see the results.

Answers come from Robot\'s own model, which reads the results and pages as information, never as instructions. History keeps the answer and the sources\' domains; titles, links and page text are never saved.
